text: Spec error-count estimate was 2.4x too low (1,861 vs 4,474 actual across 10 packages). Spec counted with tsc -b which stops early on dependency failure and undercounts; per-package fan-out revealed true scope. AF2-AF5 scoping should budget against 4,474.

architecture-critique caught a real gate-integrity hole the plan missed: when tsc crashes (OOM/invalid tsconfig) it exits non-zero with zero parseable error lines, so the naive gate would falsely PASS. Designer folded a crash guard into the plan, builder implemented it (checks raw parsed count not filtered count), review verified live. Producer/evaluator separation earned its keep.

Builder extracted a pure computeVerdict() function so the build-script gate logic is unit-testable through imports, satisfying CLAUDE.md 'tests import code' rule. 17 tests exercise 5 decision rules + 2 guards with no mocks.

Critique W2 drove dynamic package discovery (glob packages/*/tsconfig.json) replacing a hardcoded list + compensating disk-divergence guard. Gate is now self-maintaining: a new package is automatically brought under the gate.

Stale-entry ratchet is a binding contract for AF2-AF5: draining a package to zero errors requires removing its typecheck-debt.json entry in the same commit or npm run check fails. Documented with actionable failure message. Self-protecting against debt list being used to hide new debt.

Clean pipeline execution: 1 critique round (8/10, WARNINGs folded in one revision), 1 review round (DONE first pass, 3 low findings applied in one follow-up), 0 BLOCKERs, 0 NOT-DONE cycles, no reverts or WIP-cleanup commits.
